intro: Lesson 1: The modern world and why war broke out in 1914. To understand the long-term and short-term causes of the First World War

questions.q: Explain how alliances turned a local crisis into a world war.
questions.a: Each country was bound to support its allies, so when Austria-Hungary attacked Serbia, Russia, Germany, France and Britain were drawn in
questions.model: Start: Austria-Hungary attacks Serbia. Alliance link: Russia backs Serbia; Germany backs Austria-Hungary. Next: France backs Russia; Germany invades Belgium; Britain joins. So alliances spread the war.

questions.q: What does the A in MAIN stand for?

questions.a: Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to Austria-Hungary

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box, write two PEEL paragraphs: one long-term cause and the assassination.
questions.a: Paragraph 1 on a MAIN cause with evidence; paragraph 2 on the assassination as the trigger, explained
questions.model: Teacher goes through paragraph 1: 'Militarism was a long-term cause (P). Britain and Germany raced to build battleships (E). This made each fear the other and ready to fight (E). So war became more likely (L).'

questions.q: Extend: Add a judgement: which cause was most important and why?
questions.a: For example: alliances, because they turned a regional crisis into a world war

questions.q: Stretch: Why is the assassination called a 'trigger' and not the main cause?
questions.a: It started the chain, but the deeper tensions made a big war possible

questions.q: Big question: was the assassination in Sarajevo the main cause of the First World War?
questions.a: It was the trigger; the main causes were long-term: militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism
